title: Jensen Huang: Nvidia's Future, Physical AI, Rise of the Agent, Inference Explosion, AI PR Crisis
thesis: Inference, not training, is now the constraint — and the unit economics of AI have flipped: tokens are CapEx for knowledge workers, agents are the new operating system, and every industry from biology to robotics gets re-platformed in the next 3–5 years.

title: Jensen Huang – Will Nvidia's moat persist?
thesis: Nvidia's moat isn't one thing — it's the whole five-layer stack (supply chain, chips, CUDA, ecosystem, install base) compounding annually. The TPU/ASIC threat is overstated, the China export-control debate is being fought on cartoon premises, and the next leg of compute scaling comes from algorithms and segmentation, not just transistors.

title: Elon's Anthropic Deal, The Next AI Monopoly?, "FDA for AI" Panic, Trading the AI Boom
thesis: Anthropic just outran every comparable: $10B → $44B ARR in four months, with the only constraint being compute and power. The SpaceX-Anthropic deal solves that for both sides simultaneously, sets up SpaceX's IPO as a Mag-1 candidate, and shifts the AI story from 'will the revenue show up?' to 'is one company about to become the most powerful monopoly in human history?' Meanwhile the regulatory and PR backlash is building faster than the industry's response to it.

title: SpaceX's $2T Case, Nvidia's Shock Selloff, America Turns on AI, Trump Pulls AI Order, Bond Crisis?
thesis: The AI economy is simultaneously generating unprecedented value while triggering a PR and social crisis driven by dystopian layoff messaging, anti-humanist perception, and possible foreign information campaigns — with macro backdrop of 310% global debt-to-GDP and rising yields.

title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
thesis: Sutton argues LLMs are not on the path to real intelligence because they lack goals, ground truth, and learning from experience — the actual substrate of intelligence is reward-driven continual learning grounded in a world model, not imitation of human tokens.

title: Yann LeCun's $1B Bet Against LLMs
thesis: LeCun's JEPA framework solves the core failure of generative video models by predicting in embedding space rather than pixel space, and provides the world-model foundation that LLMs structurally lack for reliable agentic AI.

title: AI can't cross this line and we don't know why.
thesis: Neural scaling laws follow precise power laws across 13 orders of magnitude of compute, data, and model size, and while the manifold resolution hypothesis offers a compelling partial explanation, we still lack a unified theory for why AI performance obeys such simple mathematical rules.

title: Demis Hassabis — Scaling, superhuman AIs, AlphaZero atop LLMs, AlphaFold
thesis: Demis Hassabis argues that AGI will require layering AlphaZero-style planning and search on top of scaled LLMs, that DeepMind's 20-year project is on track for the 2030s, and that non-deception must become the foundational safety criterion before systems grow capable of self-directed improvement.

title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
thesis: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton argues LLMs are a fundamentally mistaken path to AI because they mimic people instead of learning from experience toward goals, and that true intelligence requires continual learning agents with reward, prediction, and world models — the same paradigm that defines animal cognition.

title: Yann LeCun's $1B Bet Against LLMs
thesis: LeCun argues that LLMs are a dead-end for general intelligence and that JEPA — a non-generative, joint-embedding world-model architecture — is the right substrate for agents that can predict the consequences of their actions.

title: AI can't cross this line and we don't know why.
thesis: Neural scaling laws describe a startlingly simple power-law relationship between compute, data, model size and model loss — and the manifold hypothesis offers a compelling but incomplete theoretical reason why this 'compute-efficient frontier' exists at all.

title: Demis Hassabis — Scaling, superhuman AIs, AlphaZero atop LLMs, AlphaFold
thesis: Hassabis argues the most likely path to AGI is large multimodal models used as world-model priors with AlphaZero-style planning and search bolted on top — and that DeepMind is roughly on the 20-year timeline it set in 2010.

title: Jensen Huang: Nvidia's Future, Physical AI, Rise of the Agent, Inference Explosion, AI PR Crisis
thesis: Jensen Huang argues Nvidia has evolved from a GPU company into an AI-factory company whose moat is the full CUDA stack across every compute layer, and that agentic AI plus physical AI represent a vastly larger market than analysts model — so the industry's real risk is self-inflicted doomerism, not technology.
